messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered: okta-token-verify-service - elevated token verification failures (500/401) affecting auth-proxy and console logins. Pager: mei (oncall). Link to alert: https://monitoring.redwood.dev/alerts/okta-token-verify
mei (oncall): Acknowledging, on it. First check: are we seeing a spike in 401s only, or also 5xx from our verifier?
mike: Seeing both. Quick dump from the verifier logs:
```
2026-02-12T18:12:03Z ERROR token_verifier.go:214 signature verify failed: kid not found in JWKS (kid: "a1b2c3")
2026-02-12T18:12:03Z WARN jwks_cache.go:47 JWKS cache miss for issuer https://redwood.okta.com/.well-known/jwks.json
2026-02-12T18:12:04Z ERROR auth-proxy 502 upstream token verification error
```
mei (oncall): Ok. That reads like a JWKS rotation/propagation issue on Okta side. Anyone seeing increase in console support tickets?
jenny: Yes, support queue #gfx has multiple reports: users can't SSO into console, some receive 401s. I pulled the dashboard: login success rate down ~2.7% across NA region, clustered between 18:10-18:20 UTC. Affected tenants: 12 enterprise customers (IDs redacted).
sam: Confirmed API tokens that rely on session cookies still work for existing sessions. New SSO logins failing. So scope is SSO login flow / token verification path.
eng-security: Do not relax signature verification. We should not change crypto checks. Find a safe mitigation.
mike: Two quick mitigation options I see: 1) Force a JWKS cache refresh across the fleet (clearing local caches + re-fetch) 2) Flip a feature flag to enable session-grace: allow existing cached sessions to bypass re-verification for 5m to keep console access (no new tokens granted). Thoughts?
mei (oncall): Try 1 first. Give me the command to roll JWKS cache refresh.
mike: Running rolling cache refresh now:
```
for node in $(cat /etc/redwood/nodes/okta-verifiers.txt); do 
  curl -X POST "https://$node.internal/_ops/refresh-jwks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" &
done
```
mike: Executed against 120 verifier nodes, response 200 from 118, 2 timeouts — retrying those.
mei (oncall): Monitoring auth-proxy rates...
(2m later)
mike: Partial improvement: 65% of nodes now have updated JWKS, error rate cut ~60% in NA, but still seeing failed verifications from edge nodes in eu-west.
Okta Support: Thanks for escalation, we're seeing a propagation delay in our JWKS distribution downstream to our CDN. Root cause identified, working on purging caches. Incident ref OKTA-20260212-7721. We'll post updates.
eng-security: Good to hear. We should still enable the session-grace flag in case propagation takes longer. Mike, prepare the flag but don't flip until we confirm risk.
mike: Preparing flag rollout: POST https://flags.redwood.dev/feature/session-grace {"enabled":true, "ttl_mins":5, "scope":"console"} (will do canary to 10% of console traffic first)
mei (oncall): Approve canary. Turn on for 10% now.
mike: Canary 10% turned on. Commands below:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.dev/feature/session-grace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"enabled":true,"ttl_mins":5,"scope":"console","canary_pct":10}'
```
mike: Canary looks stable for 5 minutes, console traffic success back to baseline for canary users. No errors observed.
jenny: Support update drafted: "Root cause: Okta JWKS propagation delay. Temporary mitigation applied: session-grace canary to keep existing sessions active while Okta resolves. On-call will follow up once resolution confirmed." Can we include estimated affected customer count?
mei (oncall): Put estimated impacted logins ~2-3% for the 10-minute window, ~12 customers with SSO failures. Severity: Sev2 (customer-facing, partial outage). Create INC ticket.
sam: Created INC-2026-137 with notes and Okta incident ref. Linking logs and grafana panels.
Okta Support: JWKS propagation purge in progress. Expected recovery in ~10-15 minutes. We'll confirm when CDN caches are flushed.
(10m later)
mike: Okta says purge complete. I'm scaling back the session-grace canary to 0 and initiating a cluster-wide verification: running the same refresh script with retries until all nodes report current JWKS.
mei (oncall): Good. Update support and customers: can remove temporary mitigation.
mike: Cluster-wide refresh reported success: all 120/120 nodes got updated keys. Error rates returned to baseline.
incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Severity downgraded to post-incident review.
mei (oncall): Handoff to alex for postmortem and follow-ups. Summary: root cause = Okta JWKS propagation delay -> verification failures -> SSO login failures for a subset of customers. Mitigations applied: rolling JWKS cache refresh; session-grace canary (10%) as short-lived safety; coordination with Okta support. Action items: - Alex: own postmortem, runbook updates for JWKS refresh playbook - Eng-security: review session-grace telemetry & safety guardrails - Support: customer outbound + affected-tenants list + credits if needed - Ops: add automated JWKS validation check to deployment pipeline
alex: Taking handoff. I'll draft the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with Okta contacts. Any outstanding items?
mei (oncall): No outstanding operational steps. Leaving the incident in your hands. Thanks team :white_check_mark: 
alex: Acknowledged — oncall handoff accepted. Will ping eng-security and support leads.
eng-security: We'll review the temporary flag audit logs and confirm no risky tokens were issued.
jenny: Support will start outreach to affected customers and share INC-2026-137.
mei (oncall): Closing incident channel for active paging. If Okta posts further updates we'll re-open.
